reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a 114 MW, 685,000 square foot data center in Sterling, Virginia, and the third largest of the 25 Virginia facilities that publish capacity.

The published Virginia total is 1,603 MW across 330 mapped data centers, which makes this single campus 7.1 percent of the state's disclosed IT load. That concentration is the point. A state with hundreds of mapped facilities still has only 25 that disclose a megawatt figure, so the disclosed total is a floor, not a measure. The 114 MW here is real load, not a nameplate claim, and it sits in Ashburn, inside Northern Virginia's existing power and network backbone.

For AI specifically, the useful conversion is the one the capacity supports. At 400 watts per rack for training workloads, 114 MW is roughly 285 racks, or about 2,280 high-end accelerators at 8 GPUs per rack. That is a material amount of training or serving capacity, and it is smaller than the largest US campuses. The LEED certification speaks to how the building is operated, not to how much compute it can hold.

What the data does not cover is the constraint that matters most. Grid limits on further expansion in Virginia are not published here, and neither is the facility's actual utilization, its power source, or its interconnection status. The 400 watts per rack and 8 GPUs per rack figures are stated assumptions, not measurements from this site. Read the 7.1 percent share as a share of what Virginia discloses, not of what Virginia runs.
